II. No two magnetic field lines are found to cross each other.
questions.solution:

__** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] Key Points__**

__
 
• **The space surrounding a magnet, in which magnetic force is exerted, is called a magnetic field.** If a bar magnet is placed in such a field, it will experience magnetic forces. However, the field will continue to exist even if the magnet is removed. **The direction of the magnetic field at a point is the direction of the resultant force acting on the hypothetical North Pole placed at that point. The direction of magnetic lines of force at any point gives the direction of the magnetic force on a north pole placed at that point.** Since the direction of the magnetic line of force is the direction of the force on the North Pole, so the magnetic lines of force always begin on the N-pole of a magnet and end on the S-pole of the magnet. A small magnetic compass when moved along a line of force always sets itself along the line tangential to it. So, a line drawn from the South Pole of the compass to its the North Pole indicates the direction of the magnetic field.
 
• The magnetic lines of force are closed concentric circles and hence, the starting or ending point cannot be specified exactly except the direction. Therefore, the direction of magnetic field lines outside the magnet is from North Pole to the South Pole and the direction of magnetic field lines inside the magnet is from the south pole to the north pole. Start and end cannot be found. **Hence First Statement is Incorrect**__

questions.question: 5 men can complete the same work in 8 days. 4 women can complete the same work in 12 days. In how many days can one man and 2 women complete a piece of work?
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

Total Man-days = 5 × 8 = 40 days for 1 man.

Total Woman-days = 4 × 12 = 48 days for 1 woman.

For 2 women, days = 48 ÷ 2 = 24 days.

Combined time for 1 man and 2 women = (40 × 24) ÷ (40 + 24) = 960 ÷ 64 = 15 days.

**∴ The correct answer is 15 days.**

**__Alternate Method__**

Given: 5 men finish work in 8 days; 4 women finish work in 12 days.

Formula: Total Work = Efficiency × Time

questions.question: An article is sold for ₹1,938 after two successive discounts of 15% and 5%. What was the original price of the article?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Selling Price = 1938

Discount 1 = 15%

Discount 2 = 5%

**Formula used:**

Successive Discount = Discount 1 + Discount 2 - Discount 1 × Discount 2 / 100

Selling Price = (100 - Discount)% × Marked Price

**Calculation:**

Successive Discount = Discount 1 + Discount 2 - Discount 1 × Discount 2 / 100

= 15 + 5 - 75 / 100

= 20 - 0.75

= 19.25

Selling Price = (100 - Discount)% × Marked Price

1938 = (100 - 19.25)% × Marked Price

1938 = 80.75% × Marked Price

Marked Price = 1938 / 0.8075

= 1938 × 100 × 100 / 8075

= 2400

Marked Price = ₹2,400

**Answer is ₹2,400.**

questions.question: What is the value of x in the number 3426x if the number is divisible by 6 but NOT divisible by 5?
questions.solution:
**Concept used:**

Divisibility rule for 2:

If the unit digit of a number is divisible by 2 then the number is divisible by 2.

Divisibility rule for 3:

If sum of all the digits of a number is divisible by 3 then the number is divisible by 3.

Divisibility rule for 6:

If a number is divisible by 2 and 3 both the the number is divisible by 6.

Divisibility rule for 5:

If the unit digit of a number is 5 or 0 then the number is divisible by 5.

**Calculation:**

Given number = 3426x

If this number is not a factor of 5 then the value of x must not be 0 or 5.

Now, we have to check the divisibility by 3.

Sum of all digit = 3 + 4 + 2 + 6 + x = 15 + x

The number is also divisible by 2 so x should be an even number.

15 + x = 15 + 6 = 21

21 is divisible by 3 so the number is also a factor of 6.

**∴ The correct answer is x = 6.**

questions.question: A person deposited some money at a simple interest rate for 3 years. Had he deposited the money at 2% higher rate, it would have fetched Rs. 360 more. Find the amount of the money deposited.

Extra interest is generated directly due to the extra rate for the given time.

Total extra interest % = Time × Extra rate % = 3 × 2% = 6%

This 6% of the principal corresponds to Rs. 360.

Principal (100%) = (360 ÷ 6) × 100 = 6000

**∴ The correct answer is ₹6000.**

questions.question: The sum of the ages of a mother, son and daughter is 70 years. If the mother is thrice as old as her son, and the daughter is 5 years older than her brother, how old is the mother?

Mother's age = 3 units = 3 × 13 = 39 years.

questions.question: Which of the following Articles prohibits employment of children under 14 years of age in factories?

__
 
• **Article 24** of the Indian Constitution prohibits the employment of children below the age of 14 years in factories, mines, or any other hazardous employment.
 
• This provision ensures that children are protected from exploitation and harmful work conditions.
 
• Article 24 is part of the Fundamental Rights enshrined in Part III of the Indian Constitution.
 
• The article aims to safeguard the health and development of children by preventing their engagement in hazardous occupations.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

• This Act prohibits the employment of children in certain specified hazardous occupations and processes.
 
• It regulates the conditions of work for children in non-hazardous occupations.
 
 
 
• **Article 21A**
 
 
• Article 21A of the Indian Constitution mandates the state to provide free and compulsory education to all children aged 6 to 14 years.
 
• This provision complements Article 24 by ensuring that children are in school rather than at work.
 
 
 
• **Right to Education Act, 2009**
 
 
• This Act operationalizes Article 21A and ensures every child's right to education.
 
• It mandates that private schools reserve 25% of their seats for children from economically weaker sections.
 
 
 
• **Juvenile Justice (Care and Protection of Children) Act, 2015**
 
 
• This Act provides for the care, protection, and rehabilitation of children in conflict with the law and those in need of care and protection.

questions.question: Which one of the following statements for an object falling freely under the influence of gravity is correct?

options.text: Zero acceleration always implies zero velocity
Zero acceleration has no relation with the velocity of the object
Zero velocity at any instant necessarily means zero acceleration at that instant
Acceleration is constant all throughout the free fall

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Acceleration is constant all throughout the free fall**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• An object that is moving only because of the action of gravity is said to be free-falling and its motion is described by **Newton's second law of motion**.
 
• The acceleration of the freely falling object is constant and equal to the **acceleration due to gravity**.
 
• **Acceleration due to gravity** is denoted by the symbol - **g**. 
 
• **g** = **9.8 m/s² **at sea level on the Earth.
 
• Its** SI unit **is** m/s²**.
 
• The dimensional formula is given by **[M⁰ L¹ T⁻²]**.
 
• Acceleration due to gravity is a **vector quantity**, which means it has both a magnitude and a direction.
 
• The value of **acceleration due to gravity** ‘**g**’ is affected by:-
 
 
• Altitude above the earth’s surface.
 
• Depth below the earth’s surface.
 
• The shape of the earth.
 
• Rotational motion of the earth.
 
 
 
• A free-falling object has only one external force which is the gravitational force. So it experiences constant acceleration.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Zero acceleration** does not imply zero velocity, as a body moving with a constant velocity can have zero acceleration and the body is in motion.
 
• **Zero acceleration** has a relation with the velocity of the object as it implies the body is at constant velocity.
 
• **The zero-velocity **of a body at any instant does not necessarily imply zero acceleration at that instant.
 
• The kinematic equation of motions is true only for motion in which the magnitude and the direction of acceleration are constants during the course of motion.

questions.question: Who among the following had launched the Non-cooperation Movement?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Mahatma Gandhi**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Mahatma Gandhi launched the Non-cooperation Movement in 1920 as a response to the Jallianwala Bagh massacre and the Rowlatt Act.
 
• The movement aimed to resist British rule in India through non-violent means or "Ahimsa".
 
• It was a mass protest against the British government's oppressive policies and aimed to attain self-governance or Swaraj.
 
• Gandhi urged people to withdraw their children from government schools, boycott British goods, resign from government employment, and refuse to pay taxes.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jallianwala Bagh Massacre:**

 
 
• A tragic incident that took place on April 13, 1919, in Amritsar, where British troops fired on a large crowd of unarmed Indian protesters, causing hundreds of deaths.
 
• This event marked a turning point in Indian nationalism and galvanized the Indian population against British rule.
 
 
 
• **Rowlatt Act:**
 
 
• An oppressive legislation passed by the British government in 1919 giving them the power to imprison any person suspected of terrorism without trial for up to two years.
 
• The act faced widespread opposition and was one of the catalysts for the Non-cooperation Movement.
 
 
 
• **Swaraj:**
 
 
• A term used to describe self-governance or "self-rule," which was the ultimate goal of the Indian independence movement.
 
• Gandhi's vision of Swaraj included not just political independence but also social and economic empowerment of the common people.
 
 
 
• **Ahimsa:**
 
 
• A principle of non-violence which is central to Gandhi's philosophy and strategy for the independence movement.
 
• Gandhi believed that non-violence was the most powerful weapon for oppressed people to achieve freedom and justice.
